expected_output.reasoning:
The investigation correctly identified two of the three expected patterns: (1) sqlmap/XSS/SQLi injection from 198.51.100.60 blocked by CommonRuleSet, and (2) card-testing burst on /checkout/payment from 198.51.100.30 that was only counted/allowed due to the rate-based rule being in Count mode. It also correctly identified the Artillery traffic (198.51.100.10) as benign load-test automation.

However, for the sensitive-path scan from 198.51.100.20, the investigation diverges meaningfully from the expected root cause. The expected root cause states this IP scanned ~225 distinct URIs such as /admin, /.git, /wp-login.php and that it was "mostly ALLOWED because no rule matched" — i.e., this scan mostly got through WAF. The investigation instead reports that only 25 requests matched signatures and were BLOCKED, while 200 non-matching variants were ALLOWED but "returned non-existent" (implying no real exposure), and frames this as part of a 'Recon/attack traffic ... all injection attempts blocked' narrative that downplays the fact that most of this scan passed through. This differs from the expected framing where the path scan is explicitly called out as a case WAF missed (mostly ALLOWED, no rule matched) — a key failure mode the expected root cause emphasizes as part of the overall assessment ("WAF caught the scanner-UA injection but missed the path scan and the card testing"). The investigation's summary states the opposite conclusion for recon traffic: "No injection payload reached the origin" and the finding title says "all injection attempts blocked," which contradicts the expected emphasis that the path scan got through essentially unblocked.

Given the expected root cause explicitly frames the path-scan as a case that was NOT caught (mostly allowed, no rule matched), and the investigation frames it as blocked/non-exposed, this constitutes a meaningful discrepancy in the overall root-cause characterization, even though the IP and probe types were correctly identified. This is a partial match with a conflicting conclusion on one of the three key findings.</reasoning>
